context:
Goal: git writes never run in the wrong checkout after a cd that fails, and the PR that refuses them (#2099) and the PR built on top of it (#2144) land on main.
Problem (rule): one of main's guard test cases (a cd into a missing folder, then add -A and commit) expects allow, and #2099 refuses it, so the merge tool says "Needs a ruling".
Based on (measured): a batch runner's git writes ran in the main clone after its batch folder vanished, because bash runs the commands in the start folder when the cd fails.
Based on (read): main's allow case was written for another guard's reason, a clean edit, not for this one.
Departs from: main's test expects allow — c refuses only a cd into a folder that is missing at check time.
Meanwhile: the session now carrying these PRs (the hand-off notes lane, 07:38 CST Nov 12) writes its tests on them and leaves that one case as main has it. Its proposal matches c.
home: PR #2099 (git writes after a failed cd)

options.gain: Closes the exact class of the incident.
options.how: Change main's test to expect the refusal.
options.label: Refuse every `;` after a cd
options.lose: A `;` after a cd that fails is refused even in a clean repo.

options.how: Carve this case out of the guard.
options.label: Allow it, as main's test says
options.lose: Reopens the class of the incident. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

options.gain: Closes the incident, and a `;` after a cd into a folder that exists still passes.
options.how: The guard refuses a git write after a cd only when the cd target is missing at check time; main's one test case is re-pointed.
options.label: Refuse only a cd into a missing folder (Recommended)
options.lose: Main's one test case is re-pointed, and a folder removed between the check and the run still slips.

ref: PR #2099; main's test from commit 94f68f2fa, tests/guard/s17500-conflict-markers.py:311; #2144 sits on #2099; lane fan-prose-handoffs (session_013NEJL2x8vsS7agCiTdu1LU), step notes-fix-large-3
reply: Reopened 09:10 CST Nov 10 with option c, at your request for a better option.
short: Git writes after a failed cd
title: Refuse git writes after a cd that fails, and change main's test to match?
why: Recommended: c. It closes the incident, where the folder had vanished, and still lets a `;` after a cd into a folder that exists pass.
